intake.pageTitle: Tell us what is going wrong
intake.pageBody: Describe the difficulty in your own words. Three or four questions is usually enough to find the topic underneath it — which is often not the one you would have named.
intake.constraintsBody: Set these first. They are applied by the system when tutors are shortlisted, not by the assistant.
intake.signInTitle: You will need an account for this
intake.signInBody: The conversation is saved against your account so a dropped connection resumes rather than starting again. Searching for tutors yourself needs no account at all.
intake.openingBody: For example: “My daughter is in Matric, Sindh Board, and she is weak in Maths.” Write in whichever language you prefer — English, Urdu, or a mix.
intake.resumedNote: This conversation was saved on this device and picked up where you left it.

gapMap.title: What we found
gapMap.subtitle: The topic named first is the one to teach. The others follow from it.
gapMap.chainNote: This chain comes from the curriculum itself, not from the assistant. Each topic depends on the one before it.
gapMap.unresolvedNote: These could not be settled from what was described. Answering about them would narrow it further.

constraints.heading: Applied by the system
constraints.enforcedByCode: These were applied by the search itself, in the database query, after the assistant had finished. The assistant has no way to set or relax them — the request it makes carries only the subject, level, board and topics.
constraints.notRanking: A tutor who does not meet one is not in the list at all. They are not ranked lower or shown further down.

shortlist.title: Tutors who match
shortlist.subtitle: At most three, ordered by the same score every search uses. Every figure comes from the platform’s records.

busy.title: The assistant is busy
busy.body: It is handling more than it can right now. Nothing you have written is lost, and searching directly works as normal.

unclear.title: That did not come back usable
unclear.body: The assistant’s answer could not be read. Rather than guess at what it meant, here is the direct route.

insufficient.title: We could not pin it down
insufficient.body: From what was described, the gap could not be located confidently. Saying so is better than naming a topic on a hunch — the search below is a good place to start instead.

exam.pageBody: Each topic you have claimed can be assessed on its own. Passing one adds a badge naming that topic and the date it was assessed.
exam.perTopicNote: Assessed per topic, never per subject. A topic you do not pass leaves every other claim exactly as it was.
exam.emptyBody: Add the subjects, levels and boards you teach on your profile first.
exam.startBody: Read the rules before you begin. They do not change once you start.

rules.items: Three or four written questions, on this topic only, at the level and board you claimed.
rules.graded: Your answers are read for whether they are correct, whether you explain your reasoning, and whether you pitch the explanation at a student. The mark itself is calculated by a fixed rule, not decided by the assistant.
rules.onPass: Passing adds a badge naming this topic and the date. It is valid for twelve months.
rules.onFail: Not passing changes nothing else. Your identity verification, your other topics, your profile and your bookings are untouched.
rules.override: An administrator can overturn an automated result. That is a real route, not a formality.
rules.appealOnly: This is your appeal attempt for this topic.

exam.maxExchanges: At most {{count}} exchanges in one session.
exam.answerPlaceholder: Answer as you would explain it to a student…
exam.explainHint: Explain your reasoning rather than giving only the answer, and pitch it at the student rather than at another teacher. Both are part of what is being assessed.
exam.markedInCode: The result was calculated by a fixed rule from how your answers were read. The same answers always produce the same result.

passed.title: Passed: {{topic}}
passed.body: A badge naming this topic and today’s date now appears on your profile. It is valid for twelve months.

notPassed.title: Not passed: {{topic}}
notPassed.body: This result applies to this topic only. Nothing else about your profile has changed.

appeal.overrideNote: You can appeal this. An administrator reviews the questions, your answers and the reasoning, and can overturn the automated result. Their decision is recorded with the reason.
appeal.restOfProfile: Your identity verification and every other topic you have claimed are unaffected.

exam.unavailableClaimSafe: Your claim is unchanged. Nothing was recorded against it, and you can take the assessment later.

plan.title: The plan
plan.validatedNote: The order was checked against the curriculum’s own prerequisites after the plan was written, and rewritten where it did not hold. A topic never appears before something it depends on.
plan.notValidatedNote: This plan’s order has not been confirmed against the prerequisite graph. Read it as a suggestion rather than a sequence.
plan.orderingNote: From the curriculum, not from the plan. This is what the order above was checked against.
plan.datesInCode: The dates were calculated from your start date and the exam date. The assistant ordered the topics; it did not choose any date.
plan.emptyBody: A plan is generated from a completed diagnostic and a target exam date.

countdown.heading: Until the exam
countdown.progressNote: Counted from what the tutor recorded in session notes, not from ticking topics off.
countdown.allDoneBody: Every topic in the plan has been covered and rated. Revision from here is repetition rather than new ground.

replay.body: This is a stored conversation being replayed. It is not happening now, and no AI provider is contacted when you open it.
replay.why: Built this way on purpose: a demonstration that depends on a live service is one that a rate limit can take away at the wrong moment.

demo.title: See it work
demo.body: Five recorded scenarios, each showing one thing the platform does. No account needed.
